title: Australians Thank Iraqis for Rescue Effort
description: Commodore Geoff Ledger recognizes the 2nd Battalion of the Iraqi Army for the discovery and recovery of Douglas Wood.  Soundbites from Commodore Geoff Ledger, Commander of the Australian Defense units in the Middle East and Colonel Muhammed, 2nd Battalion Commander of the Iraqi Army.  Produced by Specialist Daniel Sullivan, American Forces Network Iraq.

transcript.text: On June 15th, soldiers of the 2nd Battalion of the Iraqi Army rescued Douglas Wood, an Australian
engineer from the Hands and Terrorists.
He was being held in the Gisalia area of Baghdad.
The soldiers were part of Operation Lightning and Iraqi-led Operation.
Wood's government showed the appreciation of a nation Monday.
Well, I think it's part of the coalition showing support to the Iraqis.
Us, the Australians, showing gratification to the Iraqi Army for what they did to rescue
Douglas Wood.
You know, that was a great relief to us.
We were working with the coalition, we were working with the Iraqis to do that.
And I just think it was a fantastic effort and a feather in the cap to the Iraqi Army
that they were the ones that actually found Douglas Wood at the end of the day.
The soldiers who participated in the rescue were presented with plaques to commemorate
their bravery.
Their commander recalled the rescue, describing a success that stemmed from local intelligence
and careful planning.
We got intelligent information about Adelik Water that there are 11 suspected houses.
And perhaps there are protected people in those houses.
So I went out and checked the area by myself and we set a plan to search this area.
And a week later we went out and we discovered Douglas Wood.
In addition to firming the bonds of the coalition with the Iraqi government, the actions
of few brave Iraqi soldiers is given an Australian man a new lease on life.
Reporting for AFN Iraq, I'm specialist Daniel Sullivan.
